sake/junmai-daiginjo.explainer: The top grade: rice polished to 50% or less, nothing but rice, water, kōji and yeast. Usually delicate and aromatic.

sake/junmai-ginjo.explainer: Rice polished to 60% or less with no added alcohol. Fragrant and fruity, but with more body than a daiginjo.

sake/tokubetsu-junmai.explainer: A "special" junmai: polished to 60% or less, or made by a special method the brewery names on the label.

sake/junmai.explainer: Pure rice sake with no minimum polishing. Often fuller, richer and more savoury.

sake/daiginjo.explainer: Polished to 50% or less, with a small amount of distilled alcohol added to lift the aroma.

sake/ginjo.explainer: Polished to 60% or less, with a touch of distilled alcohol added. Light and fragrant.

sake/tokubetsu-honjozo.explainer: A "special" honjozo: polished to 60% or less, or made by a named special method.

sake/honjozo.explainer: Polished to 70% or less, with a little added alcohol for a lighter, drier finish.

sake/futsushu.explainer: Everyday table sake, made outside the premium grade rules.

sake/craft-sake.explainer: Brewed like sake but with extra ingredients such as fruit, tea or hops, or steps that take it outside the legal definition of sake. Often from new, small breweries.

sake/ungraded.explainer: Sakes whose grade hasn't been recorded yet.

makgeolli/all.explainer: Korea's cloudy rice wine: lightly sparkling, milky and often unpasteurised, brewed with nuruk.

wine/cabernet-sauvignon.explainer: Thick-skinned black grape. Firm tannins and blackcurrant.

wine/merlot.explainer: Soft, plummy red grape, rounder than Cabernet.

wine/blend.explainer: Wines made from more than one grape. Each drink page lists its grapes.

spirits/whisky.explainer: Distilled from fermented grain and aged in wooden casks.

spirits/gin.explainer: Neutral spirit flavoured with juniper and other botanicals.

spirits/brandy.explainer: Distilled from fermented fruit, here apples.

spirits/shochu.explainer: Japan's distilled spirit, made from barley, sweet potato, rice and more, with kōji.

spirits/soju.explainer: Korea's distilled spirit. Traditional versions are made with nuruk.

cocktails/highball.explainer: Spirit topped with soda over ice.

liqueur/umeshu.explainer: Japanese plum liqueur made by steeping unripe ume in alcohol and sugar.
